repairDescription: Use these built-in Windows tools to scan for and repair corrupted system files.
repairRunOrder: Run {{dism}} first to repair the component store, then {{sfc}} to fix system files.

commandCatalog.title: More diagnostic and repair commands
commandCatalog.description: Each tool shows its risk and explains the action before running. Tools requiring a disk choice or recovery startup are guidance only.
commandCatalog.completed: Command completed. Review the output for details.
commandCatalog.failed: The command could not be run.
commandCatalog.restartNeeded: Restart the computer to complete this change.

dismCheck.name: DISM — Quick check
dismCheck.simple: Checks whether Windows has recorded corruption in the system image.
dismCheck.advanced: Runs CheckHealth. Reads the recorded image state; it does not perform a full scan or change files.
dismCheck.manual: Atlas can run this command after confirmation.

dismScan.name: DISM — Full scan
dismScan.simple: Scans the Windows component store for corruption.
dismScan.advanced: Runs ScanHealth. It can take several minutes and only diagnoses; use DISM RestoreHealth above if corruption is found.
dismScan.manual: Atlas can run this command after confirmation.

dismRepair.name: DISM RestoreHealth
dismRepair.simple: Checks the Windows component store and attempts to repair it.
dismRepair.advanced: Uses local files and may use Windows Update as a repair source. This can take several minutes.

sfc.name: SFC /scannow
sfc.simple: Checks protected Windows files and replaces corrupted files when possible.
sfc.advanced: Compares system files with valid copies in the component store. For best results, run DISM RestoreHealth first.

chkdsk.name: CHKDSK /scan
chkdsk.simple: Checks the selected disk's file system for errors.
chkdsk.advanced: Runs an online scan of volume C:. It is not a physical-sector scan with /r and does not replace the drive manufacturer's diagnostics.

netshWinsock.name: NETSH — Reset Winsock
netshWinsock.simple: Attempts to fix connection problems by resetting Windows network components.
netshWinsock.advanced: May affect VPNs or software that installed network components; restart is recommended.

netshTcp.name: NETSH — Reset TCP/IP
netshTcp.simple: Resets the basic Windows network stack settings.
netshTcp.advanced: May remove custom network settings; use only if other checks did not solve the issue.

ipconfig.name: IPCONFIG — Clear DNS cache
ipconfig.simple: Clears website addresses temporarily stored by Windows.
ipconfig.advanced: Runs flushdns only. It does not change the computer's IP address or reconnect to the router.

appx.name: Get-AppXPackage / Add-AppxPackage
appx.simple: Can repair registration for a Windows app that will not open.
appx.advanced: The steps depend on the affected package. Bulk re-registering apps can produce errors; first repair the specific app in Settings.
appx.manual: Atlas does not bulk re-register apps. Repair the specific app in Settings > Apps > Installed apps > Advanced options > Repair.

winmgmtVerify.name: WINMGMT — Verify WMI
winmgmtVerify.simple: Checks whether the Windows management repository is consistent.
winmgmtVerify.advanced: Runs verifyrepository only. Verify consistency before attempting repository recovery.

winmgmtSalvage.name: WINMGMT — Salvage WMI repository
winmgmtSalvage.simple: Attempts to repair the WMI repository if verification reports inconsistency.
winmgmtSalvage.advanced: May rebuild management data. Use only after verification confirms inconsistency.

bootrec.name: BOOTREC
bootrec.simple: Helps repair problems that prevent Windows from starting.
bootrec.advanced: Runs in Windows Recovery Environment, not in a running Windows session. Incorrect options can change startup configuration.
bootrec.manual: Boot to Settings > System > Recovery > Advanced startup. Use Startup Repair; manual commands require a specific diagnosis.

bcdboot.name: BCDBOOT
bcdboot.simple: Recreates Windows boot files when the boot partition is damaged.
bcdboot.advanced: Requires identifying the Windows folder and the correct system/EFI partition. A wrong partition can make the computer unbootable.
bcdboot.manual: Atlas will not choose or modify boot partitions automatically. Use Recovery Environment with technical guidance and a backup.

reagentc.name: REAGENTC — Recovery status
reagentc.simple: Shows whether Windows Recovery Environment is enabled.
reagentc.advanced: Runs /info only. It does not change settings.

diskpart.name: DISKPART
diskpart.advanced: Some commands can erase disks or partitions. Atlas does not run disk-changing commands.
diskpart.manual: Do not run clean, delete, or format without identifying the disk and having a backup. Get technical guidance for partition changes.

vssadmin.name: VSSADMIN — List shadow copies
vssadmin.simple: Shows copies used by System Restore and backup tools.
vssadmin.advanced: Atlas only lists copies. It does not delete restore points, which could remove recovery options.

powercfg.name: POWERCFG — Power diagnostics
powercfg.simple: Checks settings that may affect sleep, battery, and power use.
powercfg.advanced: Creates a 30-second diagnostic report in a temporary folder. It does not change the power plan.

gpupdate.name: GPUPDATE
gpupdate.simple: Refreshes policies applied to the computer and user account.
gpupdate.advanced: Most useful on work or school managed computers; some policies may require logoff or restart.

wusa.name: WUSA — Uninstall update
wusa.simple: Provides the Windows option to remove a specific update.
wusa.advanced: You need to know which update (KB) caused the issue. Removing an update may remove security fixes; Atlas will not choose one automatically.
wusa.manual: Open Settings > Windows Update > Update history > Uninstall updates. Choose only the update linked to when the issue began.

fsutil.name: FSUTIL — Query USN journal
fsutil.simple: Checks the change journal for the C: file system.
fsutil.advanced: Runs a read-only query. Deleting or recreating the journal can affect indexers and backup tools.

systemreset.name: SYSTEMRESET — Recover this PC
systemreset.simple: Opens Windows options to reset or reinstall the operating system.
systemreset.advanced: A reset can remove apps and, depending on the choice, personal files. Atlas will not start a reset automatically.
systemreset.manual: Open Settings > System > Recovery > Reset this PC. Review the options and back up files first.

confirmRepairDescription: This operation checks or changes Windows system files and may require administrator privileges. Continue only if you want Atlas to start the selected repair tool.
dismCardDescription: Scans the Windows component store for corruption and repairs it using Windows Update. Run this before SFC if system files can't be repaired.
sfcCardDescription: Scans all protected Windows system files and replaces corrupted or missing files with a cached copy from the component store.
restartRecommended: A restart is recommended to complete repairs
adminRequiredSfcDesc: Relaunch Atlas as administrator to run SFC.
adminRequiredDismDesc: Relaunch Atlas as administrator to run DISM.
chkdskCardSubtitle: Check disk for file system errors
chkdskCardDescription: Scans the file system and metadata for errors. This is a non-destructive read-only scan that reports problems without making changes.
adminRequiredChkdskDesc: Relaunch Atlas as administrator to run CHKDSK.
maintenanceDescription: View connected drives and run TRIM on SSDs to tell them which areas can be reused.
trimInfoBody: TRIM tells your SSD which blocks are no longer in use so it can erase them ahead of time. The OS already does this on a schedule — running it manually only helps when that schedule has lagged. HDDs do not need TRIM.

storage.title: Storage History
storage.description: Track local folder growth and compare storage snapshots
storage.privacy: Snapshots contain folder names and size metadata only, stored locally for up to 90 days within a 250 MB budget. Global exclusions apply. Logical sizes count each file path; links, other mounted volumes and Atlas's own data are excluded. No file contents are read or uploaded.
storage.capturing: Capturing metadata since {{time}}. You can leave this page.
storage.capturingOther: Capturing metadata for {{folder}} since {{time}}. Choose that folder to review its history.
storage.projectionValue: Around {{days}} days remaining at {{growth}} of growth per day.
storage.projectionRange: Approximate model range: {{min}} to {{max}} days, based on {{count}} daily observations.
storage.noProjection: A forecast needs at least seven comparable daily observations spanning seven days and a stable positive growth trend.
storage.projectionCaution: This estimates the whole volume from free-space measurements. Other applications and folders affect it. The range describes model fit, not a guarantee or proof of what caused growth.
storage.empty: Capture a baseline to begin. Incomplete or unavailable scans are kept with their status.
storage.compareHint: Choose an earlier Before and a later After snapshot. Only complete snapshots with the same volume, folder and exclusions can be compared.
storage.overlap: Rows include parent and child folders; do not add their totals together. Added/removed paths may represent moves or renames. Folder detail is retained for three levels; sizes include deeper files.
storage.noChanges: No folder changes in this comparison.
storage.deleteScopeConfirm: Stop automatic snapshots and delete this folder's local snapshot history? The actual folder and files will not be changed.
storage.deleteConfirm: Delete this local snapshot? Comparisons using it will no longer be available. Actual files are not affected.
storage.daily: Capture daily while Atlas is running
storage.dailyHint: Checks every ten minutes. Waits for AC power, two minutes of idle time and Game Mode to finish. At most one daily attempt per folder; offline attempts are recorded. Alerts are limited to once per folder per day and respect completion notifications.
storage.growthAlert: Growth alert (GiB since previous snapshot; blank disables)

reason.limit: Stopped at the scan limit; deeper folders may be missing
reason.changed: The folder or volume changed during the scan
reason.inaccessible: Some folders could not be read
reason.excluded: The folder is covered by a global exclusion
reason.cancelled: The capture was cancelled before it finished
reason.unavailable: The folder became unavailable during the scan

comparisonReason.incomplete: Partial, cancelled or unavailable snapshots cannot support a reliable growth comparison.
comparisonReason.scope: The volume, folder, exclusions or measurement policy differ.
comparisonReason.order: Choose an After snapshot taken later than Before.

storage.emptyDescription: Choose a folder, capture a baseline, then take another snapshot to see what grew. Your files stay untouched.
